messages.subject: Question about surface alignment
parts:
Hello Geomorph community. 
I am running into a 3D alignment issue that I hope someone can help me with.
I am trying to align 3D objects using 6 fixed landmarks and (495) sliding surface semi-landmarks but I am running into an issue in that after PGA the aligned meshes no longer have the same shape (see attached figure lower panel). I am certain I must be missing a step. If I treat all of the vertices as fixed landmarks the resulting aligned mesh looks fine (see figure upper panel).

I am using the following code for gpagen: 

alignmentMixed <- gpagen(ntsfiles[,,1:5], curves = NULL, surfaces = c(7:502), PrinAxes = FALSE, max.iter = NULL, ProcD = FALSE, Proj = TRUE, print.progress = TRUE)

I've attached an image of the problem. The upper image shows the aligned result when considering all points to be fixed. The bottom image shows the same object after using surface semilandmarks as per the above code
I am not using curves but do I need to be in order to use surfaces?

Thank you for your help.
Tim Gallaher

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Question about surface alignment
parts:
Tim,

You might consider first trying the analysis with procD = TRUE, just to see what happens.  I am not advocating this as a solution, but if it seems to produce a more reasonable outcome, you might identify the problem is due to semilandmark density.

I have found that using a bending energy approach to sliders when the density of semilandmarks is high can cause this problem but using a minimized Procrustes approach does not, as it becomes essentially the same as treating the semilandmarks as fixed when there are so many.  In such cases, it might be just that the density of surface points is too extreme to try to use bending energy (presumably because the PC tangent plane used is ill-defined if points are not spread out a bit).  

I prefer using bending energy compared to minimized Procrustes distance, but at some point, trying to slide semilandmarks that are so adjacent to each other becomes an unnecessary step.  

I hope that makes sense.

Cheers!
Mike

You did mention 6 fixed landmarks with our 100, or 500, or thousands of sliders, and if those sliders are not really homologously aligned relative to the fixed points, or if the fixed points re not really fixed points, some strange things could happen. From the image you sent that is hard for me to determine. Regardless, without additional details it is just impossible to know.

 

If you email me off-line with more details of the data etc. I can try to take some time to investigate this with you.

messages.author: 3ba9c13174149f8d
messages.subject: Re: Question about surface alignment
parts:
Hello together,

today I faced a similar problem in my 2D dataset and maybe it helps if I show it to you as well.
For some reason it totally distores two out of eight curves (with 5-10 semiLM each) in one of my sampled species (n=5), creating a loop (see figure "Distortion.tif", black:mean, red:target specimen), while all other specimen (n=107) are fine (figure Otherspecies.tif). Before GPA everything looks fine. This then yields to uncorrect shape predictions in the PCA-Morphospace, creating posteriorly elongated ridges (maxPC1shape.tif) which in fact are not present in any of my samples! Neither BE nor PD sliding produced acceptable results. I checked more than ones the order of landmarks and also tried various parameters like iterations. The only reason I see is that the affected species (that are salamander crania) has a larger gap between quadratum and maxilla than all the others (see the two black LM close to each other left and right side). Hence, semiLM are more anteriorly shifted on the mouth outline and this seems to affect also the sliding of the other curves within the cranium for some reason.

Best,
Peter

Peter,

 

I suspect this has to do with how semilandmarks are being specified in your data. GPA plus sliding will not ‘invent’ patterns in some data and not others without cause; which is usually what is provided to it. However, without more information it is impossible to tell or diagnose the issue.

 

If you provide me with more information off-line I can try to carve out some time to investigate with you.

Dean
